body.input: Which companies expanded to France in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available reporting from 2026, here are notable companies that expanded to or within France during the year:

## Major Investments & Expansions

- **Amazon** — Announced a massive €15 billion investment in France (2026–2028), its largest-ever country commitment. This includes four new distribution centers, expanded AWS cloud infrastructure in the Paris area, logistics expansion in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region, and the creation of over 7,000 permanent jobs. An earlier announcement also cited a €1.2 billion investment creating 3,000 jobs as part of the "Choose France" event.

- **USA Rare Earth (USAR)** — Outlined plans to invest approximately €175 million (~$204 million) in France through 2030, expanding its metal, alloy, and magnet-making operations in the country, aligned with U.S. Commerce Department agreements to reduce reliance on Chinese rare earths.

- **Aramco Ventures** — Opened a new office in Paris to access France and Europe's innovation ecosystem, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, industrial digitization, and quantum computing. France is one of the top three venture capital markets in Europe.

- **GSK and Accenture** — Announced investments worth billions in France as part of the annual "Choose France" event.

## Tech & SaaS Expansions

- **Ideals** — Established a dedicated commercial team in Paris (announced March 2026) to support the French M&A market with its virtual data room platform, with plans to grow the office further over the following 12 months.

- **Globalstar** — Received French government regulatory clearance to launch and operate 54 next-generation direct-to-device satellites under a 20-year spectrum license. Its Satellite Operations Control Center is based in Toulouse, France.

## Logistics & Retail

- **GXO Logistics** — Expanded its partnership with Action (European non-food discounter) by opening a third distribution center in Onnaing, northern France, supporting up to 1,000 jobs and serving up to 290 stores across France and Belgium.

- **Lucid Group** — Announced plans to open its first three French retail and service sites in early 2027, as part of a network of more than 16 locations by end of 2027, signaling its entry into the French market.

- **Dinnissen** — Opened a new branch in France, giving French customers a dedicated local contact for process systems and equipment projects.

## Other Notable Activity

- **Daher Aircraft** — Inaugurated an expanded spare parts, maintenance, and logistics support facility in Jonzac-Neulles, western France (July 2026).

- **SGS** — Expanded its accredited microbiological testing capabilities at its Plouzané laboratory in France (announced January 2026).

- **SuperQ Quantum Computing** — Reported European business development activities including a keynote at the World Quantum Cannes Festival in France (November 2026).

France also saw significant data center investment from major cloud operators including **AWS, Microsoft, Google, and Oracle Cloud**, contributing to a data center market projected to reach $9.19 billion by 2031.

context.content: # Amazon to invest €15bn in France in largest-ever country commitment. Amazon has outlined plans to invest more than €15bn ($17.59bn) into France between 2026 and 2028, marking the US retailer's biggest financial commitment to the country to date. As part of the expansion, Amazon intends to open four new distribution centres and extend its existing network across the country. Amazon France country manager Jean-Baptiste Thomas said: "This investment plan of more than €15bn carries a clear ambition: to be ever more useful to the French people and the French economy. These investments will directly benefit local communities, with more than 7,000 permanent jobs created, while allowing the French businesses that rely on our marketplace, technologies, and cloud and AI solutions to grow.". The company has been present in France for 25 years and has channelled more than €30bn into the country since 2010 across logistics, technology, and operations. "Amazon to invest €15bn in France in largest-ever country commitment" was originally created and published by Retail Insight Network, a GlobalData owned brand.

STOCKHOLM (Reuters) - Amazon said on Monday it would invest more than 1.2 billion euros ($1.3 billion) in its French operations and create more than 3,000 permanent jobs in the country. The French presidency had said on Sunday that Amazon and other companies, including GSK and Accenture, would announce investments worth billions as part of the country's annual "Choose France" event, which begins on Monday. Amazon Web Services' (AWS) investment would increase cloud infrastructure in the Paris area to support France's flourishing generative AI opportunity, and logistics infrastructure in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region, the company said in a statement. Amazon has invested more than 20 billion euros in its French operations since 2010 and employs more than 22,000 permanent employees across its cloud and online retail businesses. "These jobs are in addition to the 2,000 jobs we announced for 2024," said Frédéric Duval, country manager at Amazon France.

# France Approves Globalstar to Launch 54 Next-Gen D2D Satellites Under 20-Year Spectrum License

PARIS — The French government has granted regulatory clearance for satellite telecommunications operator Globalstar to launch and operate its constellation of 54 next-generation direct-to-device satellites, SpaceNews reported on Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026.

The regulatory decision authorizes Globalstar’s C-3 network, filed with the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) under the network identifier AST-NG-C-3, to access and operate across global Mobile Satellite Services (MSS) spectrum allocations for a 20-year term. [...] Engineered specifically to support direct-to-device cellular connectivity and high-reliability emergency messaging, the C-3 space architecture matches the orbital geometry of Globalstar’s legacy constellation. Prime contractor MDA Space is manufacturing the 54 spacecraft, which comprise 48 active operational low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites and six dedicated on-orbit spares.

Each satellite will operate at an orbital altitude of 1,414 kilometers, incorporating active beamforming S-band payloads to communicate directly with standard hand-held mobile devices. Flight operations will be commanded through Globalstar’s dedicated Satellite Operations Control Center in Toulouse, France, alongside its primary control facility in Covington, Louisiana.

Launch Manifest and 2027 In-Orbit Deployment [...] Launch Manifest and 2027 In-Orbit Deployment

Globalstar targets the inaugural orbital launches of the C-3 constellation starting next year in 2027. Under the French space decree, the operator is authorized to conduct space flight operations across the full 13-year design lifetime of the satellites, providing service continuity for consumer mobile networks and sovereign applications.

## Footer

Satnews is a leading provider of satellite news, events, publications, research and other satellite industry information in both commercial and military enterprises worldwide.
